articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from WWE and AEW.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from WWE and AEW.

WrestleMania 43 Cost Reportedly Revealed

WWE is reportedly set to cash in big after bringing WrestleMania 43 to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, next year.

During a recent episode of Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer revealed WWE's expected payday for the marquee show.

"I actually just found this out, like this morning. It looks like the WrestleMania price is $150 million," Meltzer said (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News). "I knew it was over 100 because people in Saudi Arabia told me it's north of $100 million. [They usually] get 55 [million] to go. It's $150 million for WrestleMania. And that is, you know, you don't want to put that in jeopardy."

WrestleMania 43 is expected to take place on April 10 and April 11, 2027. While it's still far away, there are reportedly questions about whether sporting events in the region will move forward.

"There's a UFC show in Saudi Arabia November 28th or December 5th, which I would say that's in jeopardy," Meltzer said. "There's the Canelo fight, which has not been canceled yet, but there's certainly lots of talk about it."

Still, Meltzer said that WWE will have a hard time walking away from a $150 million payday, regardless of the pushback the company may receive.

Drew McIntyre Addresses Retirement Speculation

Longtime WWE veteran Drew McIntyre has been absent during his recent Hollywood pursuits, but that doesn't mean his wrestling career is nearing its end.

During an appearance on Stephanie McMahon's What's Your Story? podcast, McIntyre made it clear that his budding acting career won't stop him from continuing his run in WWE.

"This is home. I'm not going anywhere," McIntyre said (h/t H. Jenkins of Ringside News). "This is like we have an understanding of talking with Nick and Paul (Levesque) that if something good comes up, we do that. But I'm a full-time wrestler. I just turned 41."

McIntyre hasn't been seen in WWE since losing to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42 in April, as he's turned his attention to filming outside projects, including Highlander and Agent of Shadows .

Still, McIntyre reiterated that he plans to stick around in WWE for the foreseeable future.

"I'm going to be here for years," he said. "So don't expect me to disappear anytime soon."

AEW's Ilja Dragunov Opens Up About WWE Departure

After making his AEW debut at Saturday's WrestleDream pay-per-view, former WWE Superstar Ilja Dragunov had a unique way of explaining why he left his former company.

Dragunov told reporters at the post-show scrum that he wasn't satisfied with the competition level he had previously faced, leading to his decision to join AEW.

"I have this urge to fight. I love to fight, and I want to compete, and I want to step up. If I feel that the air in a certain environment gets thinner for me, I need to breathe. That's what I did today, here," Dragunov said. "If I need a place to breathe new, fresh air, see a new landscape, and see what the world can offer me to satisfy this hunger for competition. That's the easiest answer I can give you to that question."

Dragunov departed WWE after his contract expired in August, and while his AEW debut was in the works for a while, he almost didn't make it. Dave Meltzer reported on Wrestling Observer Radio that visa issues tied to Dragunov's previous WWE employment nearly delayed his coming-out party, but once AEW aired a vignette teasing his arrival, it was clear that it was sorted.

"They had the vignette ready and they knew it was going to be any day now, but they didn't want to put it on if he wasn't going to be at the pay-per-view," Meltzer said (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News). "I mean, the plan and the hope absolutely was for him to be on the pay-per-view."

Dragunov's arrival adds an exciting young Superstar to AEW's already impressive roster of talent, and it will be fun to watch his climb to the top.

articles.title: Why Now is The Time For WWE to End The Judgment Day Faction Once and For All
articles.summary: The Judgment Day have officially worn out their welcome in WWE.
articles.body:
The Judgment Day have officially worn out their welcome in WWE.

A case can even be made that the mere existence of the faction is doing more to hinder than help everyone still in it.

That's a strange statement to make when two of the members currently hold gold and the group gets more screen time than almost anyone on Raw most weeks, but that's exactly why it's time for WWE to call it quits with them.

They're overexposed, uninteresting and stuck in the same stories. Liv Morgan and Stephanie Vaquer have been at odds over the Women's World Championship since February, Dominik Mysterio has been feuding with his father Rey Mysterio on and off for four years, and the rest of Judgment Day are treading water.

Raw could use a significant shakeup in the worst way, and breaking up Judgment Day once and for all could be what benefits both the brand and everyone associated with the stable.

Liv Morgan Isn't Evolving as a Character

Liv Morgan replacing Rhea Ripley as the unofficial face of The Judgment Day in the summer of 2024 was the best thing that could have happened to her and the group at the time.

The incarnation of the stable with Ripley, Damian Priest, Dominik Mysterio, Finn Bálor and JD McDonagh was peak Judgment Day, but it had also run its course. Ripley and Priest had already begun to embrace the audience as babyfaces, so removing them from their ranks gave the group a fresh coat of paint.

It also put Morgan in a prominent position on Raw for the first time in her career, a spot she has shined in ever since. Her stock skyrocketed, and within a matter of months, she was one of the most popular performers—male or female—in the entire company.

As such, it made sense for her to win the Women's World Championship at WrestleMania 42. Unfortunately, the fallout left a lot to be desired, and she went until SummerSlam four months later without defending her title.

Stephanie Vaquer regaining the gold in her native Chile was a fun moment, but all it ended up being was just that: a moment. She won back the belt at Money in the Bank not long after, and currently, there aren't any obvious challengers waiting in the wings.

She's stuck doing the same shtick and being bogged down by Judgment Day isn't doing her or the title any favors.

Roxanne Perez Has Been Ready to Break Out for Months

Liv Morgan getting back the Women's World Championship at Money in the Bank would have been fine had Roxanne Perez won the women's Money in the Bank Ladder match earlier in the evening.

That would have allowed Perez to subtly tease tension with Morgan and plant the seeds for an eventual (successful) cash-in on her. Perez and Morgan weren't exactly on the same page in the wake of WrestleMania 42, but their dissension was quickly forgotten about and never acknowledged again.

Perez was the perfect addition to Judgment Day in 2025. She had just been called up to the main roster from NXT and the group served as a vehicle to introduce her to the audience in an organic way, not to mention she instantly had chemistry with everyone already in the faction.

At this point, she has become more of a background player than anything else. Although she beat Chelsea Green in non-title action on the Oct. 12 edition of Raw, there's virtually zero chance she wins the WWE Women's Championship from her in their eventual rematch.

Morgan vs. Perez being the ultimate endgame is acceptable, but it shouldn't be taking this long to get there.

WWE as a whole has been very faction-heavy since Triple H took the reins of WWE Creative in mid-2022, though most of the stables that once dominated SmackDown have since migrated over to Raw.

The Bloodline have obviously been a focal point of the flagship show this year, along with The 946 as part of their ongoing rivalry with the Roman Reigns-led group. The Vision, for some reason, still have a presence on the program as well and remain relevant largely thanks to Bron Breakker and Bronson Reed.

That has automatically made The Judgment Day the fourth-most important stable on the show, and arguably the least interesting.

Additionally, all four factions are heel (The Bloodline are babyfaces only when WWE wants them to be), so there is zero reason for them to existing simultaneously.

The faction warfare on Raw has grown tiresome and has led to lazy booking and storytelling. It forces certain Superstars into feuds where nothing is being accomplished, so pulling the plug on Judgment Day would free up television time and afford others the opportunity to get over with the audience.

Raquel Rodriguez's Women's Intercontinental Championship Is Irrelevant

The Women's Intercontinental Championship was at its most coveted whenever it was in the possession of Becky Lynch. She successfully elevated it to the next level through her feuds with Lyra Valkyria, Maxxine Dupri and AJ Lee in the latter half of 2025 and the first quarter of 2026.

The title quickly lost a lot of relevance once Lynch lost it to Sol Ruca at Clash in Italy and abruptly disappeared from programming. Ruca had one televised title defense against Raquel Rodriguez in June before dropping it to her in a rematch at the end of July.

Rodriguez won their rubber match in August with the gold once again on the line, but the belt has not been defended on WWE TV otherwise since then. Rather, it's been treated like a total prop in The Judgment Day with the Women's World Championship taking precedence.

Raw's midcard women's division are more concerned with fighting with the faction in meaningless multi-person matches instead of challenging for the championship. Becoming the champ was a cool accolade for Rodriguez, but the title serves no purpose around her waist if she isn't going to be doing anything of note with it.

The Women's Intercontinental title has been well worse off in the time it's been held hostage by Judgment Day, and ridding Raw of the group would get the belt back in matches that matter.

Dominik Mysterio Is Currently an Afterthought

It's astonishing to see just how far Dominik Mysterio has fallen from where he was at this time one year ago in WWE to where he finds himself on the card today.

The third-generation star walked out of WrestleMania 41 with a ton of momentum as the new Intercontinental champion. He went on to have a memorable run and beat a slew of Superstars in the remainder of the year, including John Cena.

The abysmal booking of Mysterio in 2026, however, has been nothing short of bizarre.

He lost the Intercontinental title in March followed by the AAA Mega Championship in September, he failed in his feuds with Finn Bálor and Danhausen, and couldn't even qualify for the men's Money in the Bank Ladder match.

He's currently as directionless as he's ever been and has shown no signs as of late of entering anything remotely consequential. He's instead being relegated to being a punchline in promos involving Liv Morgan.

At the age of 29, Mysterio has his entire career ahead of him and can still ascend to main event stardom someday, but after doing so much to get him where he is today, it's The Judgment Day that's holding him back from fulfilling his full potential.

What's Left for Judgment Day to Accomplish?

The Judgment Day first formed in April 2022 when Edge enlisted the help of Damian Priest to defeat AJ Styles at WrestleMania 38. After being on the brink of collapse, the supernatural-esque stable evolved into something so much more once Edge was excommunicated in favor of Finn Bálor a few months later.

They experienced their most success between early 2023 and mid-2024 by holding the World Heavyweight Championship, the Women's World Championship, the Undisputed WWE Tag Team Championship, the NXT North American Championship and the men's Money in the Bank briefcase, sometimes simultaneously. They also headlined Survivor Series 2023 in a WarGames match.

They've gone through several periods of dissension, resulting in Edge, Priest, Ripley and Bálor being betrayed and removed from the faction over time. If that's what awaits the likes of Liv Morgan and Roxanne Perez, it would be no different than the same story they've told before.

Judgment Day will go down as one of the most decorated and accomplished groups in WWE history, but after almost five years, there's nothing left for them to do. Not even shifting them over to SmackDown at this stage would be enough to make them feel fresh again.

Adding more members isn't the answer, either. With WWE having gotten all it possibly can out of Judgment Day and then some, the next step is building toward their imminent split.

WarGames Must Be the Beginning of the End

All signs point to WWE holding two WarGames matches again this year: one for the men and one for the women. The Bloodline and The 946 are bound to have the men's matchup on lock, but the women's installment could easily be occupied by the remaining female members of The Judgment Day.

There's been a bit of faction warfare with the women on SmackDown in recent months, but there's a stronger story to tell with the ladies of Raw inside WarGames, specifically with Liv Morgan and Roxanne Perez not being able to coexist and that being the catalyst behind Judgment Day's demise.

Judgment Day have no shortage of enemies in the women's division at the moment between Lola Vice, Sol Ruca, Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch. Other women can logically be added to fill out the five-on-five format, but the focus should primarily be on Judgment Day and Perez no longer wanting to fall in line.

The group has always turned on anyone on the verge of breaking off on their own, so Perez should be the first to sever ties with them before it happens to her. The rest of the faction can gradually dissipate from there with Perez moving on to bigger and better things as a babyface.

The Judgment Day deserve a proper payoff for how pivotal they've been to Raw since 2022, but to drag it out much longer will squander any equity the group has left.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: European Championship Darts: Luke Littler to face William O'Connor in opener as Gian van Veen starts defence vs Andrew Gilding
articles.summary: The European Championship Darts begins in Dortmund on Thursday October 22, with Luke Littler facing Ireland's William O'Connor in first round; Defending champion Gian van Veen plays Andrew Gilding; watch the Grand Slam of Darts live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
World champion Littler, who won two of the three European Tour events he played in this year, will seek to arrest a poor run of form which has seen him lose in the quarter-finals of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, in the first round at the World Grand Prix and the semi-finals of the World Youth Championship.

Littler had been hoping to add the World Series of Darts, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals trophies to complete a historic clean sweep of the year. But his bid was derailed by Jonny Clayton in the Netherlands.

Dutch No 1 Van Veen - who set a new record average on the European Tour this weekend - has fond memories of Dortmund as he secured his maiden Premier title 12 months ago before his run to the World Championship final in January.

The 24-year-old has enjoyed a successful year on the European Tour, making the final of the season opener in Poland as well as three consecutive semi-final runs in the last three events.

Following the conclusion of the Dutch Darts Championship on Sunday, which saw Niels Zonneveld secure his first-ever European Tour title, the 32-player field for the European Championship was confirmed, with seedings based on the one-year European Tour rankings.

That victory means Zonneveld will now start his hunt for a Premier title as fourth seed and will take on Cameron Menzies.

World No 2 and last year's runner-up Luke Humphries kicks off his campaign as the 12th seed and will face Ryan Searle.

Ross Smith - a winner of two European Tour titles this year - enters as the top seed and will take on Karel Sedlacek.

Wessel Nijman will compete as second seed after also boasting two titles on the circuit this year and he will meet Germany's Martin Schindler.

Other notable ties include 2019 runner-up Gerwyn Price vs two-time champion Rob Cross , Kevin Doets against four-time champion Michael van Gerwen and 2018 winner James Wade against Damon Heta.

The action gets under way at Dortmund's Westfalenhallen on Thursday, with a top prize of £150,000 up for grabs on Sunday October 25.

articles.title: Cristian Toro será el número cinco de VOX por Madrid al Congreso
articles.standfirst: La regatista Ángela Pumariega y el waterpolista Víctor Gutiérrez van en las listas del PP y PSOE a las elecciones generales, respectivamente
articles.summary: La regatista Ángela Pumariega y el waterpolista Víctor Gutiérrez van en las listas del PP y PSOE a las elecciones generales, respectivamente
articles.body: En plena cuenta atrás para las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, los partidos políticos van desvelando los nombres de sus listas. En la nómina de candidatos al Congreso de los Diputados, ya aparecen algunos vinculados al ámbito deportivo como los campeones olímpicos Ángela Pumariega y Cristian Toro o el waterpolista Víctor Gutiérrez. Este lunes se ha sabido que Toro, campeón olímpico en Río 2016 en el K2 200 junto a Saúl Craviotto, será el número cinco de VOX por Madrid al Congreso. El ex palista es en la actualidad portavoz nacional de Deportes del partido encabezado por Santiago Abascal. El piragüista fichó por VOX en 2023 como número 6 de su lista al ayuntamiento de Madrid de cara a las elecciones municipales y autonómicas de aquel año. "Sentía que era un paso que tenía que dar por mis principios y por la gestión que está habiendo últimamente. Creo que los más jóvenes tenemos que ponernos al frente de las ideas que creemos que son correctas y esta es la oportunidad que he visto para defender las ideas y los valores en los que confío", dijo entonces en una entrevista a MARCA. "No podemos ir regalando nacionalidades" fue uno de los titulares que dejó. Pumariega, oro olímpico junto a Támara Echegoyen y Sofía Toro en la clase Elloit 6M en Londres 2012, es la actual concejala de Economía, Empleo, Turismo e Innovación de Gijón. Ayer se anunció que la ex regatista asturiana encabezará la candidatura del PP al Congreso por Asturias. Licenciada en Economía y Máster en Coaching y Liderazgo Deportivo, entró en la corporación gijonesa como edil del Partido Popular en el año 2019 y en 2023, tras ser candidata a la Alcaldía, asumió la vicealcaldía. "Estoy muy ilusionada con la propuesta y por la confianza", dijo ante los medios al conocerse la noticia. Y el waterpolista Víctor Gutiérrez concurre como el número 13 del PSOE por Madrid al Congreso de entre los 38 candidatos socialistas. En octubre de 2021 fue nombrado Secretario de Políticas LGTBI de la Comisión Ejecutiva Federal del PSOE. Tomó posesión como diputado en el Congreso por Madrid en diciembre de 2023 Diputado de la XV Legislatura, con doble grado Periodismo y Comunicación Audiovisual (URJC) y Máster Comunicación Corporativa, Eventos y Protocolo (ESERP), Gutiérrez fue fichado por Sánchez en la pasada legislatura en la que ya concurrió en el puesto 13 de la lista. En las elecciones generales no son tantos los deportistas que concurren en las listas al Congreso y Senado, pero en las últimas elecciones autonómicas, numerosos rostros del ámbito deportivo formaron parte de los listados: Roberto Sotomayor, Mayte Martínez, Eva Arias, Javier Cienfuegos, Adelardo Rodríguez, Carlos Pérez, Dani Molina, Kini Carrasco, Eliseo Martín, Gonzalo Colsa, Jesús Tortosa, Laura Nicholls, Miriam Gutiérrez...

articles.title: Debating Triple H's Obsession With WWE's Survivor Series WarGames Match
articles.summary: WWE will once again present Survivor Series: War Games this year, live from Houston's Daikin Stadium on November 28.
articles.body:
WWE will once again present Survivor Series: War Games this year, live from Houston's Daikin Stadium on November 28.

The two-ring, steel cage war of attrition has become a staple of the pro wrestling calendar, but should it be, or has its yearly usage at the big-four premium live event watered down its effectiveness?

Let's debate each side of the argument, including Triple H's seeming obsession with keeping it on the schedule, and come to a conclusion.

The Fall months in WWE have long been the doldrums.

Yes, the creative team may introduce story threads that will ultimately culminate at WrestleMania, but there has always been a sense of the mundane and lackluster when it comes to the post-SummerSlam months in WWE.

So much so that the company routinely sought a gimmick it could book its annual Survivor Series around. First, it was the traditional tag team elimination match. Then it was the survivors match, featuring the surviving members of each team competing in one big, final bout.

There was the Deadly Game tournament and brand warfare before Triple H introduced War Games as a main event marketing tool.

Since then, the match has helped Survivor Series regain prestige as one of WWE's elite shows of the year, while also paying off long-running rivalries that have dominated airwaves for months. It worked well for The Bloodline story in 2022 and again a year later, when Cody Rhodes and Co. faced The Judgment Day.

It is a match that has enough built-up history, thanks to its usage in similar situations during the height of NWA and Jim Crockett Promotions, and has produced memorable moments and quality matches to justify its place on the card.

It has also emphasized the importance of factions in WWE, and if history teaches us anything, it is that factions, groups, trios, and the like allow for more creative opportunities and, as a result, better TV.

Look no further than the aforementioned Bloodline and Judgment Day, both of whom, at their peaks, were central and driving forces on Raw and SmackDown.

Once upon a time, Hell in a Cell had its own premium live event.

Every year, without fail, WWE would trot out the event, headlined by matches that lacked the hate or longevity around them to justify taking place in the namesake steel structure.

The result was diminishing returns and the long-overdue elimination of the event from the WWE schedule in 2022.

The show had so watered down the Hell in a Cell concept that it took a legitimate, long-running rivalry with legitimate dislike between the competitors to justify bringing it back, which Triple H and his creative team did in October of 2024 when CM Punk and Drew McIntyre delivered an instant classic at Bad Blood.

While this year's event is an exception, thanks to the excellently crafted Bloodline vs. 946 feud, the War Games match risks the same overexposure.

Just like it did in NXT, when its introduction meant the conclusion of a long-running or intensely personal, faction-based rivalry, it became a staple of the Survivor Series amid the height of the Bloodline story. It served a purpose involving The Judgment Day, too.

Over the years, in both the developmental and main roster brands, the continued promotion of the War Games match has spoiled the creative direction of some of the top feuds in WWE.

There is no question about where programs are heading, and as a result, the excitement that once existed is in danger of wearing off.

The moment The Bloodline and 946 began feuding, it was abundantly clear that the creative team was booking toward Survivor Series. While it is absolutely a positive for the writers to have an endgame in mind and a direction to take stories, there is a certain level of predictability that can settle in.

That predictability, added to the overexposure and saturation of the match type given the inclusion of a men's and women's match each November, threatens to water down its effectiveness.

There is a certain level of diminishing returns that WWE has to be careful with when it comes to War Games. There was undeniable damage done to Hell in a Cell during its run as an annual PLE centerpiece, and it is interesting, to say the least, that the guy who moved to preserve the importance of that gimmick match has opted to do the same with the two-ring steel cage war.

With that said, Triple H has succeeded as a booker when he can utilize multi-person matches to introduce stories, advance them, or culminate them.

We have seen it consistently throughout his run at the top of the company, where he has planted the seeds for some rivalries, written the conclusions of others, and introduced feuds that would carry through to WrestleMania.

It has been his major creative playground.

That the show has only really produced one stinker (2025, I'm looking at you), there is still an argument for it remaining a part of the PLE schedule.

If the 2026 show disappoints, though, especially with The Bloodline vs. 946 figuring the headline the show, this conclusion will warrant revisiting.

articles.title: España y Euskadi se medirán en la final femenina de cesta punta del Mundial
articles.standfirst: Erika Mugartegui y Arai Lejardi se enfrentarán a las vascas Maite Ortiz de Mendibil y Eneritz Lizardi
articles.summary: Erika Mugartegui y Arai Lejardi se enfrentarán a las vascas Maite Ortiz de Mendibil y Eneritz Lizardi
articles.body: España y Euskadi se jugarán el título mundial femenino de cesta punta. La final en el frontón de 54 metros será el primer duelo entre dos pelotaris españolas contra dos vascas por un título en este campeonato del Mundo de Pelota que se celebra en Buenos Aires (Argentina). La lucha por el oro será una reedición del último partido de la fase de grupos de esta disciplina, una de las nueves presentes en este Mundial. En dicho choque, Erika Mugartegui y Arai Lejardi, ambas de Markina (Vizcaya) y que hace un año decidieron jugar por España en vez de por Euskadi, se impusieron a las vascas Maite Ortiz de Mendibil y Eneritz Lizardi por 15-6 y 15-3. Las dos parejas fueron las mejores en esta fase y se verán las caras con el oro en juego. En categoría masculina, los pelotaris vascos Xabier Barandika y Unai Lekerika también estarán en la final. Tras ganar a la dupla francesa por un doble 15-6 se medirán en la final a los hermanos estadounidenses Sorozabal (Johan y Gorka) que en el último duelo de la fase de grupos vencieron a los españoles por 15-10 y 15-12. En la primera fase, los estadounidenses ya se impusieron a Barandika y Lekerika. Este Mundial de Pelota es el primero con el País Vasco como miembro de pleno derecho de la Federación Internacional. En el anterior Mundial, disputado en octubre de 2022 en Biarritz (Francia), España lideró el medallero con 20 metales (nueve oros, nueve platas y dos bronces), Francia fue segunda con 16, cinco de oro, y México, tercera con 10.

Team: Penn State Nittany Lions Sport: College Football Venue: Beaver Stadium

Origin Story: The 1948 Cotton Bowl carried significance beyond just the result on the field, as Penn State was asked to leave its two Black players—Wally Triplett and Dennie Hoggard—at home for the matchup with SMU in Dallas, Texas. The Nittany Lions refused, with team captain Steve Suhey reportedly saying "We're Penn State" to illustrate the team's unity. The game moved forward, and Triplett and Hoggard became the first Black players to appear in the Cotton Bowl.

Modern Role: In the mid-1970s, the Penn State cheerleading squad created the modern call-and-response of "We Are..." and "...Penn State," though it took years to catch on and become the stadium-wide chant that it is today. It has effectively transcended the football team and sports in general to become the universal greeting of Penn State alumni.

Team: Nashville Predators Sport: NHL Venue: Bridgestone Arena

Origin Story: During the Predators' inaugural 1998-99 season, local bar owner Bob Wolf wanted a Tennessee-inspired version of the Detroit Red Wings' octopus toss for the fledgling franchise. Wolf reportedly bought a nine-pound catfish, wrapped it in newspaper and smuggled it into the arena under a baggy jersey, hurling it onto the ice when the Predators scored their first goal.

Modern Role: The catfish toss has been a franchise staple since 2003, though etiquette surrounding it has evolved. It is now mostly reserved for the postseason and rivalry games, and catfish are generally thrown after the national anthem and before the puck is dropped to avoid potential delay of game penalties for the Predators. Bridgestone Arena even features a live catfish tank, as the team has fully embraced the tradition.

Origin Story: Cowbells found their way into Mississippi State athletics sometime during the 1930s and 1940s. Legend has it a cow wandered onto the field during a Mississippi State victory over arch-rival Ole Miss and quickly became a good-luck charm. Cows were brought to subsequent games until that practice was scrapped in favor of the cowbell, and the tradition grew in the 1960s when long-handled cowbells became a staple in the university bookstore.

Modern Role: In 1974, the SEC voted 9-1 to ban artificial noisemakers from sporting events. That ban held until 2010, when the topic was revisited and an exception was made for the Mississippi State cowbells, with strict rules. They can be rung during pregame, halftime, timeouts and immediately following scoring plays, with violations resulting in a potential fine to the university.

Team: Ole Miss Rebels Sport: College Football Venue: University of Mississippi campus

Origin Story: The Grove is a 10-acre plot of land in the center of the Ole Miss campus, and in the 1950s it started to become a popular tailgating spot ahead of football games. Until 1991, fans drove vehicles into the area as they would any other tailgating spot, but a significant rain storm turned the area into a swampy mess and vehicles were officially banned.

Modern Role: The vehicle ban transformed the tradition into a unique village of pop-up tailgating tents, and standard tailgating has been scrapped in favor of Sunday-best attire and upscale cuisine. The "Walk of Champions" is the pinnacle of the tailgating event. Roughly two hours before the game, the entire football team makes its way through the crowd along a designated brick path, a tradition that began in 1983 with head coach Billy Brewer.

Team: Auburn Tigers Sport: College Football Venue: Jordan-Hare Stadium

Origin Story: In 1962, Sewell Hall opened as the new residence hall for the Auburn football team. As players walked the path from their dorm to the stadium, kids began lining the route to ask for autographs. The tradition shifted in 1989, when rival Alabama played the Iron Bowl on-campus at Auburn for the first time after previously meeting at a neutral site. The Tiger Walk path was lined with an estimated 20,000 fans, and the tradition was changed forever.

Modern Role: Auburn players and coaches are now taken by bus to the corner of Donahue and Samford at 2.5 hours before kickoff for the Tiger Walk. It is widely regarded as the gold standard of a pregame tradition that has become a staple across college football, and Tiger Walk Plaza further highlights the longstanding tradition.

Team: Cincinnati Reds Sport: MLB Venue: Great American Ball Park

Origin Story: The 1869 Cincinnati Red Stockings were the first professional baseball team, and to honor that legacy, Major League Baseball generally scheduled the Reds to host the first game and throw the first pitch of each new MLB season. In 1920, merchants at Findlay Market held a celebration of the team's 1919 World Series title, and organized a one-mile march to Redland Field to await the first pitch of the 1920 season.

Modern Role: The Findlay Market Opening Day Parade is now an annual tradition, drawing over 100,000 annual spectators, and it has turned into an unofficial holiday in the surrounding area. Modern scheduling often means the Reds don't throw the official first pitch of the season, but they still almost always open the year with a home series.

Team: Arkansas Razorbacks Sport: College Football Venue: Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium

Origin Story: A group of farmers attending an Arkansas football game in the 1920s began squealing like hogs to try to encourage a struggling team, and when they pulled out the victory a tradition was born. The next game, a more organized chant was developed, and the "Woo Pig Sooie" cheer was born.

Modern Role: The cheer is now accompanied by precise choreography, as fans start with an eight-second "Woooo" while raising their hands over their head, drop them and form a fist for "Pig" and raise their fist into the air for "Sooie" with that cadence repeated three times before the "Razorbacks" closer.

Team: New Orleans Saints Sport: NFL Venue: Caesars Superdome

Origin Story: The phrase "Who dat?" has roots in 19th century vaudeville shows, and later in early jazz and big band music. On Sept. 1, 1983, local New Orleans sports anchor Ron Swoboda aired a high-energy clip of local high school team St. Augustine chanting "Who dat talkin' bout beatin' St. Aug?" and three days later the chant spontaneously broke out at the Superdome in the Saints' season opener.

Modern Role: Saints head coach Bum Phillips fully embraced the cultural phenomenon during the 1983 season, and it quickly became a rallying cry for the Saints. The chant took on more formal mechanics during the Drew Brees era, and now before every home game kickoff, a designated player or celebrity guest leads the chant at midfield.

Team: Chicago Cubs Sport: MLB Venue: Wrigley Field

Origin Story: WGN Radio director Dan Fabian asked folk singer Steve Goodman to record a song for the station's 1984 broadcast of Cubs games. The catchy, upbeat tune played throughout the '84 season, which culminated in the team's first trip to the playoffs since 1945. The team would rotate through a variety of different victory songs in the years that followed.

Modern Role: The song was dusted off during the team's back-to-back division titles in 2007 and 2008, becoming a post-game singalong tradition at Wrigley Field following every Cubs win. Almost a decade later, it became indelibly linked to the long-awaited 2016 World Series title, and continues to play after every Wrigley Field victory.

Team: Texas A&M Aggies Sport: College Football Venue: Kyle Field

Origin Story: Yell Practice began as a post-dinner activity at Texas A&M in 1913, but it was not until 1931 that the midnight aspect was introduced. A group of freshmen gathered at Puryear Hall decided to meet late at night to practice their cheers ahead of a matchup with rival Texas. Senior yell leaders were informed, and while they could not authorize it, they hinted that they might show up anyway. Word spread throughout campus and Midnight Yell Practice was born.

Modern Role: Now held at midnight on Friday night before every home game at Kyle Field, roughly 25,000 fans regularly attend Midnight Yell Practice for what is quite literally a rehearsal. The 30-minute event ends with stadium lights being shut off and attendees kissing their dates for good luck.

Venue: Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium

Origin Story: The origins of the terminology date back to the 1889 Oklahoma Land Run, as "boomers" were the people petitioning the government to open up the territory for settlement, while "sooners" were those who snuck across the border illegally in advance to claim the best land before it was officially opened up. In the early 1900s, the terms were set to music with a fight song created by mashing up Yale's "Boola Boola" and North Carolina's "I'm a Tar Heel Born" reworked with Oklahoma-centric lyrics.

Modern Role: The marching band now plays "Boomer Sooner" constantly during home games, while the crowd volleys a call-and-response of "Boomer!" and "Sooner!" back and forth across the stadium.

Team: Duke Blue Devils Sport: College Basketball Venue: Cameron Indoor Stadium

Origin Story: Since the mid-1980s, the Duke student section has taken a more organized approach to heckling the opposition than perhaps any other fan base in sports. Early iterations of the "dirt sheets" on the opposing roster were no holds barred, but the university and head coach Mike Krzyzewski eventually intervened and a more academic approach was adopted.

Modern Role: With the rise of the internet in the late 1990s and early 2000s, digging up dirt on the opposition and getting the student section organized became significantly easier. Before tipoff, students are given a printed research packet of information and the contents are deployed as needed throughout the game when a player steps to the free throw line or approaches the sidelines.

Team: Sacramento Kings Sport: NBA Venue: Golden 1 Center

Origin Story: Inspired by the large halo illuminated by the Los Angeles Angels after home wins, Kings president of business operations John Rinehart pitched the concept of a similar victory illumination to owner Vivek Ranadivé. They ultimately landed on a high-powered RGB laser projection system that could project a purple beacon hundreds of feet into the air.

Modern Role: The concept was unveiled to the public on Sept. 16, 2022, and the laser was officially activated for the first time on Oct. 29, 2022, following a victory over the Heat. The lighting of the beam has now become a post-game tradition after victories, with a chosen player, coach or celebrity given the honor of pressing a giant, glowing button as the laser is activated.

36. "Take Me Out to the Ball Game" Guest Conductor

Origin Story: Legendary Cubs broadcaster Harry Caray spent years leading a stadium-wide sing-along of "Take Me Out to the Ball Game" during the seventh-inning stretch of games at Wrigley Field. Following his passing in February 1998, the Cubs wanted to preserve the tradition and lined up a series of celebrities and local figures to serve as guest conductors. His widow, Dutchie Caray, was the first guest conductor on Opening Day in 1998.

Modern Role: A long list of celebrities and athletes have taken their turn as guest conductors, though the Cubs eventually shifted to focusing mostly on people with a concrete tie to the city of Chicago or the Cubs organization. In lieu of a guest conductor, they also occasionally play clips of performances from Caray on the video board.

Team: Miami Hurricanes Sport: College Football Venue: Hard Rock Stadium

Origin Story: The University of Miami used a green block "M" with an orange outline as its primary athletics logo from 1928 until 1973 when they unveiled the iconic "Split U" logo. It was not until 1992 that cheerleader Bill Tigano was credited with popularizing the actual gesture of throwing up the U, as a response of sorts to Florida's "Gator Chomp" and Florida State's "Tomahawk Chop" to give Miami its own visual symbol.

Modern Role: The popularity of Miami football and the long list of former players who went on to prominence in the NFL have helped the symbol transcend college football game day. From fans in the stands to the surrounding Miami community, it stands as one of the most recognizable and iconic gestures in all of sports.

Team: Buffalo Bills Sport: NFL Venue: Digital

Origin Story: On New Year's Eve 2017, Bengals quarterback Andy Dalton threw a game-winning touchdown pass against the Ravens, and in the process punched the Bills' ticket to the postseason. To show their appreciation, Bills fans flooded the Andy and Jordan Dalton Foundation with $17 donations to match the 17-year playoff drought he had helped snap. The grassroots campaign ended up raising more than $400,000, and the charity blitz idea was born.

Modern Role: Subsequent charity blitzes have been run for a variety of reasons, including one in support of Lamar Jackson's preferred charity Blessings in a Backpack after he suffered a concussion against Buffalo in the playoffs. They also raised millions of dollars for the Chasing M's Foundation in the wake of Damar Hamlin's on-field cardiac arrest.

Team: Philadelphia Eagles Sport: NFL Venue: South Philadelphia

Origin Story: After incidents stemming from light pole climbing and a downed traffic signal during the Phillies' run to a World Series title in 2008, Philadelphia city officials began greasing poles with petroleum jelly to deter climbers the following year. Not just celebratory hijinks, pole-climbing actually has deep roots in the area, as the South 9th Street Italian Market Festival has featured a 30-foot greased pole climb that dates back to the 1960s.

Modern Role: The pole-greasing took center stage during the Eagles' Super Bowl run in 2018, with shortening and hydraulic fluid applied to poles ahead of the NFC Championship Game and Super Bowl. It has ultimately had the opposite of the intended impact, serving as an enticing challenge rather than a deterrent to would-be climbers.

Team: Duke Blue Devils Sport: College Basketball Venue: outside Cameron Indoor Stadium

Origin Story: On Feb. 27, 1986, a group of Duke students decided to get a jump on securing seats to the upcoming basketball game against rival North Carolina by pitching tents outside Cameron Indoor Stadium. The game was not until March 2, but they stuck it out, and Duke coach Mike Krzyzewski unofficially endorsed the act when he brought them pizza. One of the students taped a hand-written "Krzyzewskiville" sign to a post, and a fledgling tradition had a name.

Modern Role: From chaotic, free-for-all beginnings, Krzyzewskiville has become a finely-tuned machine with a full set of rules and regulations. It has also swelled from that initial three-night campout to a multi-tiered system that is a six-week rite of passage for some. The tradition has survived beyond Coach K's retirement, but the tent city will forever be Krzyzewskiville.

Team: Cleveland Browns Sport: NFL Venue: Huntington Bank Field

Origin Story: During training camp in 1985, Browns cornerbacks Hanford Dixon and Frank Minnifield started barking at each other whenever the defense would record a sack or force an incompletion. The practice spread throughout the defense and eventually into the stands, as fans started barking along. Prior to the start of the preseason, Dixon and Minnifield painted a sign that read "Dawg Country, No Cats Allowed" and hung it in front of the east bleachers at Cleveland Municipal Stadium.

Modern Role: The fans sitting in the east bleachers were quickly deemed The Dawg Pound, and they gained a reputation as some of the most dedicated fans in football. Barking, dog masks and comically large bones are all staples. The tradition continues at the team's new stadium, with Sections 118-122 and Sections 317-323 making up the current Dawg Pound.

articles.title: Thekla No-Sells Mercedes Mone At AEW WrestleDream 2026 Amid Social Media Frenzy
articles.summary: Thekla's actions outside of the ring after her loss to Mercedes Mone has fans talking.
articles.body:
Thekla and Mercedes Mone had one of the better matches of an entertaining AEW WrestleDream 2026 , but it's Thekla's actions after the match that have fans talking.

Following a pinfall loss to Mone after taking the Mone Maker, Thekla was seen rolling out of the ring and throwing up two middle fingers as she danced her way up the aisle. Wrestlers are generally expected to "play dead," and sell their opponent's offense after any hard-fought match, let alone a world title match that went 15 minutes.

In today's surveillance era, where smartphone cameras are ubiquitous, many fans took notice of Thekla's post-match actions, which drew a wide range of reactions on social media from amusement to some suggesting the Toxic Spider was being disrespectful.

"LMAOOOO Thekla not selling the finish of the match. I love her. [sic]," read one post.

"What happened here? Anyway, Thekla should have sold the damage from Mercedes Moné's finisher," said another Twitter account.

Thekla No-Sells Mercedes Mone Match At AEW WrestleDream 2026 | Fan Reaction

Thekla Vs. Mercedes Mone Escalates Amid Social Media Speculation

Further fanning the flames of the Thekla vs. Mercedes feud, Mercedes Mone seemed to dismiss her otherwise strong match against Thekla during the WrestleDream 2026 media scrum.

"Uh, I mean, it's not one of my favorite matches," said Mercedes before seeming to deliver an in-character response to her rival. "I told you guys that I'm not scared of a little spider. She's more like a chihuahua that doesn't stop talking and just (makes chihuahua noises.)"

"She's not toxic ," Mercedes continued. "I'm sick of toxic people."

"Mercedes Mone flat out buried Thekla. I'm crying son," read a tweet in response to Mercedes' apparent jab.

Whether or not Mercedes Mone and Thekla have any real-life animosity remains to be seen, but it doesn't matter if that's how fans perceive it. One of the oldest phrases in professional wrestling is "personal issues draw money." Typically that quote speaks to the spirit of simulated drama, but if real-life issues can be safely incorporated into wrestling storylines, all the better.

Charlotte Flair and Becky Lynch famously went off script during a belt exchange ceremony on SmackDown in 2021. In what was supposed to be an innocuous exchange of championship belts with both stars switching brands, tensions ensued when Charlotte Flair dropped the WWE Raw Women's Championship on the ring mat. While the moment soured their once-tight bond, it led to increased interest in their ensuing Survivor Series match.

"We were supposed to exchange the titles. I grab it out of her hand unknowingly, I'm 'Becky Two Belts' for a second then I toss her the title, then she tells Sonya (Deville) to pick it up. Then she challenges me to a fight, and I back out of it and I go. So everybody was supposed to get their moment there," said Lynch of how the segment was supposed to go before it went left.

"The title dropped," explained Charlotte. "I didn't drop it on purpose."

"If anyone knows how important the [WWE Raw women's title] is to me—I would never be dismissive of the title in the way that it was presented that I did."

AEW is no stranger to backstage drama. CM Punk's Brawl Out / Brawl In saga remains the subject of some of AEW's most notorious lore. Punk's yearlong crashout on his ex-employer continues to be the subject of heated discussions within the wrestling community.

Punk returned to WWE for an unlikely and successful run that continues to this day. Social media continues to speculate about Thekla and Mercedes Mone, and if there's more to their feud than meets the eye. This is half the battle in a wrestling promotion's goal to engage an audience.

The other half is to remain professional enough to do business in the ring.

articles.title: Broncos have 7 players on injured reserve going into Week 7
articles.summary: The Broncos have seven players on injured reserve going into Week 7.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos have seven players on injured as they approach Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season, but that number could easily change this week.

Four of those players — wide receiver Pat Bryant ( ankle ), running back Jonah Coleman ( ankle ), offensive tackle Frank Crum and tight end Caleb Lohner — are on short-term injured reserve, which means they are eligible to return after four games (although Lohner is expected to be out until at least mid-season ).

Coleman is eligible to return from IR this week , and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss might be a candidate for IR after he was spotted using a walking boot and crutches over the weekend.

Another player, offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo , is on the reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. He is also eligible to return after four games.

Denver has three players on season-ending IR: center Michael Deiter ( quad ), defensive end Matt Henningsen ( Achilles ) and linebacker Levelle Bailey ( broken leg ). The club cut linebacker Drew Sanders from IR before Week 1.

articles.title: Ben Johnson explains decision to pull Bears starters in fourth quarter
articles.summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson explains the decision to take numerous defensive starters out in the fourth quarter vs. the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
Right at the beginning of the fourth quarter, kicker Cairo Santos kicked a 50-yard field goal to extend the Chicago Bears ' lead to 31-7 against the Atlanta Falcons. Even though it was still technically a three-possession game and the entire fourth quarter was left, head coach Ben Johnson decided to put some of Chicago's depth players in, especially on defense.

Doing so allowed the Falcons to get back into the game and make it an eight-point game. Atlanta got the ball back with 3:34 left on the clock and the chance to tie up the game if they were able to score a touchdown and a two-point conversion. While cornerback Kyler Gordon was ultimately able to force a fumble, which effectively sealed the victory for the Bears , it still never should have gotten this close.

After the game, Johnson explained the decision to pull defensive starters early in the fourth quarter, which was impacted by the fact that Chicago is playing again on Thursday night against the New England Patriots.

Photos from Bears' 31-23 win over Falcons in Week 6

"You're trying to thread the needle a little bit. If we didn't have the Thursday night game, I don't know that we'd do things like we did," Johnson said. "So that's part of the equation. I do believe if we hadn't had that fumble on offense, that maybe we would've gotten out of there the way that we wanted to," Johnson said. "But things happen, and we've got to keep playing. We know that's the case, especially with an offense like that. Once again, we're trying to thread the needle and do what's best for us. Not just [that] we had to win this game first and foremost, which we did. But of course, we want to think long term also."

Both the Bears and the Patriots will come into the game with a 4-2 record coming off wins in Week 6. New England quarterback Drake Maye had three touchdown passes in their most recent victory and now has 10 touchdowns in the last three games. So, Chicago's defense will have their work cut out for them.

articles.title: Analyzing how Raiders RG Caleb Rogers played in Week 6
articles.summary: Analyzing how Las Vegas Raiders offensive lineman Caleb Rogers played in Week 6 after earning the start at RG.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders suffered a nailbiting loss in Week 6 , losing a thriller 33-30 to the Buffalo Bills . One of the intriguing pregame storylines is that Caleb Rogers was named the starter at right guard. Head coach Klint Kubiak decided to start Rogers ahead of usual starter Jackson Powers-Johnson.

Rogers did not necessarily play well after also struggling in Week 4 . The former Texas Tech standout was credited with allowing two pressures in pass protection. He was also whistled for a penalty.

Rogers didn't fare any better as a run blocker. The sophomore guard was consistently beaten in the trenches by the Bills' interior defensive linemen. The Raiders did not run the football effectively. They were outgained by the Bills on the ground 103-65. Ashton Jeanty was limited to 22 rushing yards and a touchdown on 10 carries, averaging 2.2 yards per carry. Jeanty had more receiving yards (36) than rushing.

Coach Kubiak will have to review the tape and assess his decision to reward Rogers with a start. Left guard Spencer Burford was the Raiders' best guard in this game. After the coaching staff reviews how Rogers performed, they'll have to decide whether to start him or Powers-Johnson versus the Los Angeles Rams in Week 7.

articles.summary: Morgan Rogers has hailed Morgan Rogers’ work rate and hunger as the pair continue to link up nicely in attack for the Blues.If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverag...
articles.body:
Morgan Rogers has hailed Morgan Rogers' work rate and hunger as the pair continue to link up nicely in attack for the Blues.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Chelsea's attack have carried this team at times in the early stages of this season, so on Saturday it was a relief to see a player who wasn't Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer or Morgan Rogers get the goals that earned the team a win.

It was a relatively quiet day for that front three in fact, but speaking after the game Rogers was clear on how impressed he was by striker Joao Pedro, who he hadn't played with until this season.

Joao Pedro (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

"I think his hunger to score goals, his hunger to work for the team is massive," Rogers said in quotes featured on the Chelsea official website.

"Especially for me, where I play on the pitch, it really helps me loads. He always gives me an option. I can always play off him; he can play off me.

"I think he's a massive part of us, not just scoring goals as well; he works so hard. The relentless running in the channel and working defensively as well for the team."

All three of them are working hard and attacking with quality. It's a recipe for certain success.

A lot of Chelsea fans will be watching Tottenham tonight as they face Coventry – while the Blues are resting after winning on Saturday.

Chelsea's central defenders had their best game of the season so far against Everton, mainly thanks to the protection they got from the midfield ahead of them.

articles.title: Ale Galán y la trampa de la zona de confort
articles.summary: La opinión de Jesús Mata
articles.body: Tres torneos seguidos sin una final bastan para que el pádel empiece a hacerse preguntas. Rotterdam, Düsseldorf y ahora Milán han dejado a Chingalán en una posición muy delicada ante el número 1, quizás antes de lo esperado, y eso hace inevitable plantearse si el proyecto de Ale Galán y Fede Chingotto está empezando a dar síntomas de desgaste. Antes de caer el sábado ante Lebrón y Augsburger en las semifinales del Milán P1, Galán fue bastante claro: "Hay Chingalán para rato". Conviene quedarse con sus palabras antes de imaginar rupturas que todavía no existen y, sobre todo pensar aquello de "qué va a decir...". Dicho esto, también es lógico que la gente se empiece a hacer preguntas. Galán tiene 30 años, está a punto de ser padre y sabe que el tiempo para volver a ser número uno no es infinito. Si además encadena tres torneos sin alcanzar una final, es normal que pueda preguntarse si necesita algo diferente para dar ese último paso. Ahí está la dificultad de la decisión. No está eligiendo entre una pareja que funciona y otra que no, sino entre una pareja que funciona muy bien y la posibilidad de encontrar otra que pueda funcionar todavía mejor. Puede buscar otro derecha, como Yanguas, como Jon, como Libaak, como los que queráis, y asumir el riesgo de empezar de nuevo, pero también puede seguir al lado de Chingotto, el jugador al que él mismo ha definido en varias ocasiones como "el mejor compañero que he tenido". Sobre todo, con el que ha alcanzado un nivel alienígena. Y aquí es donde creo que merece la pena detenerse en una idea que damos demasiado por hecha: que cambiar es siempre más ambicioso que quedarse. Llevo años escuchando que hay que salir de la zona de confort, que para crecer hay que incomodarse y que asumir riesgos es casi una obligación para quien quiere llegar más lejos. Pero, al menos para mí, estar en una zona de confort no significa necesariamente haberse acomodado. A veces significa haber encontrado un lugar desde el que puedes seguir creciendo sin necesidad de empezar de cero. Eso es lo que tiene Galán con Chingotto. Una pareja que ha ganado mucho y que ha conseguido construir un entendimiento en pista que no aparece de un día para otro. Galán conoce el juego de Fede, sabe qué puede esperar de él cuando llegan los momentos complicados y juntos han encontrado una manera de competir que les ha permitido estar durante mucho tiempo en la pelea por todo. Romper eso puede llevarle a algo mejor, pero también puede hacerle perder una fórmula que ya conoce. Por supuesto que tres torneos sin una final desgastan, por supuesto que quedarse otra vez a las puertas del trono del pádel te deja tocado. Especialmente a un jugador como Galán, que no juega solo para estar entre los mejores, sino para volver a ser el número uno. Precisamente por eso la decisión tiene tanto interés: no se trata únicamente de qué compañero puede darle más posibilidades de ganar, sino de qué quiere priorizar Galán en este momento de su vida. Hace unos años quizá la respuesta habría sido más sencilla. Si existe la posibilidad de mejorar, hay que intentarlo. Ahora hay más elementos encima de la mesa, como los familiares antes citados, y sobre todo que ha encontrado en Chingotto un compañero con el que está bien y con el que ya ha demostrado que puede ganar. Quizá el número uno siga siendo igual de importante, pero eso no significa que tenga que ser lo único que importe. Se puede querer ganar y no sentir la necesidad de cambiar de pareja cada vez que los resultados se tuercen. Se puede querer ser el mejor y preferir hacerlo junto a alguien con quien sabes que puedes competir. La ambición no tiene por qué medirse únicamente por la cantidad de riesgo que estás dispuesto a asumir. Por eso no compro la idea de que seguir con Chingotto sería la opción conservadora y buscar otro derecha, la valiente. Las dos decisiones implican un riesgo distinto. Una consiste en apostar por un proyecto que ya conoce pese a que los últimos resultados hayan abierto dudas; la otra, en renunciar a él con la esperanza de encontrar una fórmula mejor. Y quizá esa sea la verdadera cuestión que tiene ahora Galán delante. No si debe cambiar porque lleva tres torneos sin jugar una final y porque se quede de nuevo a las puertas del gran objetivo, sino si considera que lo que tiene con Chingotto ya no le permite llegar donde quiere. Si la respuesta es sí, tendrá todo el sentido que se la juegue. Pero si la respuesta es no, tampoco debería necesitar una justificación para quedarse. Porque creo que después de tantos años rodeados de falsos gurús diciéndonos que hay que salir de esa zona por la que has estado peleando tanto tiempo, quizá también haya que aceptar que, en ocasiones, la decisión más ambiciosa es saber cuándo merece la pena quedarse.

articles.title: How Nick Herbig tapped into 'Hungry Herb' to dominate Tampa
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers pass rusher Nick Herbig revisited his college film to ignite a game-ending two-sack performance against Tampa Bay.
articles.body:
When Pittsburgh Steelers edge defender Nick Herbig took over in the fourth quarter during a thrilling road victory, his game-ending two-sack performance looked like pure instinct. But behind that explosive effort was a deliberate mental reset born in the film room.

That mental reset could come none too soon for Herbig, who received a massive four-year, $100 million extension this past offseason. The fans expected big things from Herbig coming into the season and were beginning to get frustrated by the lack of splash. However, his two-sack performance has Steelers fans hopeful everyone is settling into this new defense.

Appearing on Cameron Heyward's podcast " Not Just Football with Cam Heyward ," Herbig opened up about the unusual preparation habit that helped unlock his relentless edge rush. He dug into his college archives at Wisconsin to reconnect with his rawest, most aggressive self.

"Just kind of getting off the rock and blacking out, bro," Herbig explained when asked what triggered his performance. "Just getting back in the archives and just, you know, watching film from three years ago, seeing how like, Young Herb, Hungry Herb, you know, sometimes you got to do that and remind yourself how you got here and don't lose that."

For young pass rushers in the NFL, technical refinement can sometimes lead to overthinking at the line of scrimmage. By revisiting film of "Young Herb," the second-year defender reminded himself that his primary weapon is sheer, unadulterated explosive speed off the snap.

Herbig took that simplified mindset directly to his veteran teammates along the defensive front, focusing on execution over complex processing.

"So, you know, just talks to Teej [T.J. Watt] and Alex [Highsmith] and T.J. just basically get off the rock, figure it out later type of joke," Herbig said. "So, it obviously worked. Got it done. Yes, sir."

The approach paid immediate dividends. Pittsburgh's pass rush clamped down late in the game, securing a walk-off sack to seal the comeback victory. As the Steelers continue navigating grueling road stretches, Herbig's blend of nostalgia and relentless "blackout" intensity gives Pittsburgh's pass-rush rotation a terrifying second wave behind T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith.
